_note: NH Picks: projects NEAR Hunt recommends, chosen from AI reviews of their repositories. Scores and memos are from NEAR Hunt's AI reviewer, not official hackathon judging. Sorted by track, then name. Generated by scripts/picks-export.mjs; selection rules in lib/picks.mjs.

picks.name: Arras
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live zero-access-key USDC escrow and proof-of-payment rating protocol actively used by Execution Market.
picks.memo:
Arras delivers a three-layer agent-to-agent hiring, non-custodial USDC escrow, and proof-of-payment reputation protocol live on **NEAR mainnet** (`v2.arras-escrow.near`). A payer locks USDC via `ft_transfer_call`, an operator (Execution Market) releases on approval or disputes settle via on-chain arbiter, humans can fund capped budgets spent by restricted agent keys, and the escrow contract holds zero access keys. Execution Market has actively routed NEAR tasks through `v2.arras-escrow.near` since 2026-11-13.

Minimal hype, clean Rust contracts, real mainnet production usage, and a clear security posture.

picks.name: Bakeoff
picks.pitch: Mainnet-proven AI workflow bounty market where agents compete via MCP, OutLayer enclaves score hidden tests, and NEAR pays winners.
picks.memo:
Bakeoff turns AI workflow optimization into an open, verifiable bounty market on NEAR mainnet: a team posts a goal against its agent's baseline, competing builders/agents submit via an MCP server, an OutLayer enclave scores submissions on hidden test cases, and the NEAR contract pays the reward only when every requirement passes. The README cites a real mainnet end-to-end run where a Claude Code agent beat a 128 µ$/ticket triage baseline on its first sealed submission.

The Rust + TypeScript repo (`contract`, `evaluator`, `mcp`, `web`, `integration-tests`, CI) tackles the hardest problem in the Agent Economy—verifying quality on hidden evals without leaking test data—and proves it on mainnet.

picks.name: Byline
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live (`byline.near`) non-transferable NFT + sub-account identity for AI agents that attaches referral/memo attribution to NEAR Intents swaps and payments.
picks.memo:
Byline is **live on NEAR mainnet** (`www.by-line.xyz` + `byline.near`) and solves agent identity + builder monetization in one stroke: minting gives an agent a non-transferable NFT + `k7m2x9qa.byline.near` sub-account, every NEAR Intents swap carries it as `referral` (paying the builder!), and every payment builds a public on-chain credit history.

Live mainnet deployment + clever Intents referral loop makes this a standout in Agent Economy.

picks.name: Horkos
picks.pitch: Rust verify-then-pay agent escrow on NEAR with NFT order receipts, TEE delivery checks, and 10k-sequence invariant tests.
picks.memo:
Horkos is a verify-then-pay escrow contract on NEAR for AI agent purchases: each order locks funds as an NFT receipt, and the seller is paid only if the owner's spending mandate permits the order and a TEE verifier confirms the delivery satisfies a machine-checkable condition; otherwise the agent is refunded.

The engineering discipline here is standout: CI runs 8 adversarial attack scenarios refused on both v1 and v2 (`attacks.rs`) alongside invariant checks over 10,000 random sequences per version, backed by `JUDGES.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `gateway/`, and `evidence/`. The main gap in the README snippet is no hosted interactive web URL.

picks.name: Judge on NEAR
picks.pitch: Encrypted agent-work escrow judged inside OutLayer Intel TDX so payment and decryption key release atomically.
picks.memo:
Directly relevant to what we're building! Judge on NEAR solves the agent-work escrow deadlock: worker delivers encrypted work, a deterministic judge program runs inside OutLayer's Intel TDX TEE, and one NEAR transaction either pays the worker + reveals the decryption key or refunds the buyer.

Highlighting Job 9—where a worker tried prompt-injecting the grader to ignore checks and got caught (score 50, buyer refunded), reproducible locally with `node jn.mjs verify`—is super compelling.

picks.name: NEAR STREAM
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live per-second agent payment streaming with autonomous watchdog/guardian freeze-and-refund.
picks.memo:
NEAR Stream lets payers stream money per second to AI agents and APIs only while a watchdog agent verifies delivery on-chain; if service breaks, payment freezes and a guardian agent refunds the payer with no human in the loop.

Crucially, it is **live on NEAR mainnet** (`85401b22...5d98`) with real NEAR execution recorded in `mainnet-evidence.json`, a read-only `npm run verify` passing 35/35 checks (including 5 mainnet checks), 31 JS + 2 browser + 5 Rust tests, and a live GitHub Pages testnet app.

picks.name: ProofStream
picks.pitch: NEAR milestone escrow releasing payouts via OutLayer Intel TDX fact checks and conservative dual-AI review.
picks.memo:
ProofStream automates open-source bug bounty and milestone payouts on NEAR testnet (`proofstream-v1.testnet`, reproducible commit `068742e`): a merged PR must pass hard-fact checks inside an Intel TDX enclave on **OutLayer** and receive completion scores from two independent AI reviewers from different model vendors/owners—with the contract paying the *lower* of the two shares.

Crucially, 12 real milestones have already executed on testnet across full pay, partial pay, refusal, hold, funder release, and refund. The conservative min-of-two payout rule and OutLayer TEE grounding make this production-minded.

picks.name: Proven: pay for what passes
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR escrow marketplace where OutLayer TEEs run planted-fake-vetted acceptance checks to pay workers deterministically.
picks.memo:
Proven is live on NEAR mainnet (`useproven.xyz`) with a razor-sharp mechanism: buyers fund a job alongside a hidden executable acceptance check—and before funds can lock, the check must catch planted fake answers. Workers (human or AI) deliver, the check runs inside an attested OutLayer TEE, and escrow pays or refunds deterministically from that result alone—no LLM judge can be talked past. It also supports GitHub PR bounties.

The repo (`contracts/`, `verifier/`, `pr-bounty-verifier/`, `relay/`, `agent/`, `skills/`, `web/`) and live mainnet deployment make Proven one of the very best builds in Batch Y.

picks.name: Psephex
picks.pitch: 2-of-3 multi-model TEE dispute jury for AI agent escrow on NEAR with a published npm MCP server.
picks.memo:
Psephex tackles agent-to-agent dispute resolution cleanly: both sides submit evidence, three independent models evaluate inside TEEs, and the NEAR contract checks 2-of-3 consensus before releasing payout. Shipping docs.psephex.xyz, a live testnet app, CI, and a published npm MCP server (@unitynodes/psephex-mcp) shows serious execution.

The main open question is cost and latency of running 3 TEE model calls per dispute on small micro-tasks, plus testnet-only status—but as an Agent Economy primitive, it's very complete.

picks.name: Recourse
picks.pitch: Bonded AI agent insurance on NEAR using `ecrecover`-verified NEAR AI Cloud TEE receipts, Sputnik DAO arbiters, and Intents refunds.
picks.memo:
Recourse builds 'insurance for AI agents on NEAR': before taking a paid job, an agent posts a bond and an underwriter vault co-signs for a premium; every job produces a NEAR AI Cloud TEE receipt verified on-chain via `ecrecover`; if work fails, the agent and vault are slashed and the client is refunded in their chosen token/chain via NEAR Intents, with a Sputnik DAO council overseeing bonded arbiters.

The repo engineering is standout—`Dockerfile.judge`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DECISION.md`, `SECURITY.md`, YouTube walkthrough, and a live zero-install demo (`recourse-near.duckdns.org`). A cohesive, multi-primitive Agent Economy architecture.

picks.name: Snow Moon
picks.pitch: Mainnet USDC escrow where NEAR AI workers hire `market.near.ai` agents via x402 and verify results in OutLayer TEE.
picks.memo:
SnowMoon is an autonomous agent-to-agent commerce and escrow protocol live on **NEAR mainnet** (`core.cryptozax.near`). A user locks USDC in `JobVault`, a budget-matched NEAR AI Cloud lead agent routes the job, autonomously hires and pays specialized `market.near.ai` agents over **x402 (USDC)**, verifies the output through an **OutLayer TEE** worker, and settles on-chain after user preview and approval. Includes `near/`, `outlayer-worker/`, `snowmoon/`, live app (`snowmoon.website`), and X video demo.

Combining mainnet USDC escrow, x402 sub-hiring, and OutLayer TEE verification makes it one of the most complete full-stack NEAR agent builds in the batch.

picks.name: Sphinx
picks.pitch: Mainnet proof-paid agent marketplace verifying Intel TDX test grades on-chain with Base-to-NEAR-to-Avalanche settlement.
picks.memo:
Sphinx is the standout Agent Economy build in Batch C: an AI agent is paid only when its code passes hidden tests graded inside an Intel TDX enclave, and the NEAR mainnet contract verifies Intel's attestation on-chain before releasing funds. Better yet, it has a real recorded mainnet run (`deployments/runs/mainnet2-job8.json`): a buyer paid USDC from Base, the agent passed 32/32 tests, received 1.425 NEAR 31 seconds after submission, and cashed out to 7.12 USDT on Avalanche. It also ships `SKILL.md`, `llms.txt`, and `CLAIMS.md`.

There is no glaring weakness—this is production-grade cross-chain + TEE + NEAR mainnet execution.

picks.name: Antibody
picks.pitch: Executable bug bounties where OutLayer Intel TDX enclaves re-run exploit proofs and pay out on-chain.
picks.memo:
Antibody starts from a sharp real-world pain—curl shutting down its bug bounty over AI-slop reports—and replaces text reports with executable exploit proofs. A hunter submits exploit code, an OutLayer Intel TDX enclave re-runs it against the project's committed invariants, and a critical break pays out automatically and pauses the protocol.

The repo depth (formal/, golden/, fixtures/, CLI + verifier Dockerfiles, CI, JUDGES.md) is exceptional. Main limitation is that real-world protocols still need deterministic reproduction harnesses, which is hard outside sandboxed contracts.

picks.name: Aruna
picks.pitch: Discovers NEAR global-contract silent-upgrade blind spots and classifies account mutability from 3 public RPC reads.
picks.memo:
Aruna uncovers and operationalizes a genuine NEAR-specific security blind spot: an account running a *global contract* published by another account can silently execute new code when the publisher redeploys, with no transaction touching the account and `view_account.code_hash` remaining `11111111111111111111111111111111`. Aruna classifies any NEAR account into one of four mutability classes from three public RPC reads and gives agents a keyless pre-send guard.

Ships a reproducible monorepo (`apps/`, `contracts/`, `lab/`, `measurement/`, `fixtures/`, `SECURITY.md`) and live site (`arunafi.xyz`). Genuine protocol-level insight.

picks.name: AttestGuard
picks.pitch: On-chain NEAR spend-envelope firewall that verifies NEAR AI Cloud Intel TDX enclave approvals before releasing agent funds.
picks.memo:
AttestGuard pairs an on-chain NEAR spend-envelope contract with a reviewer model running inside NEAR AI Cloud's Intel TDX enclave. Rather than relying solely on static amount caps, the contract verifies the enclave key's signature on-chain—binding the payment approval to a specific TDX-attested inference result—so a prompt-injected agent trying to wire $7K to an unknown wallet is blocked while a legitimate $3K invoice settles.

The repo is well-organized (`contracts/`, `verifier/`, `frontend/`, `tests/`, `docs/`, `SUBMISSION.md`, CI workflow) and includes a testnet console screenshot and X demo video. While it remains testnet-only and relies on NEAR AI Cloud's enclave trust root, it pushes past basic allowlist/cap contracts by verifying TEE-backed intent reasoning on-chain.

picks.name: Baret
picks.pitch: Pre-signing NEAR transaction analyzer (`safe`/`caution`/`blocked`) paired with a keyless function-call-key vault live on mainnet.
picks.memo:
Baret goes beyond static spending caps by simulating and inspecting every NEAR transaction against live chain state *before* an agent signs—returning `safe`, `caution`, or `blocked` with explicit reasons for sneaky attacks like adding a full-access key in a batch, calling the vault to raise its own limit, paying a 1-hour-old or flagged account, or a NEAR Intents quote paying out elsewhere—backed by a keyless mainnet vault.

Live on NEAR mainnet, clean monorepo (`apps/`, `packages/`, `contracts/`, `SECURITY.md`, CI), and directly addresses why naive spending caps fail.

picks.name: Bursar
picks.pitch: AI invoice treasurer ('the AI reads, the contract decides, a dumb executor moves the money') with 67 unit tests and NEAR AI Cloud TEE reading.
picks.memo:
Bursar's separation of duties—'the AI reads (in NEAR AI Cloud TEE), the contract decides, a dumb executor moves the money'—is super crisp. Shipping 67 policy-contract unit tests, 3 documented security review rounds, a live console/explorer at bursar.network, and a full whitepaper shows serious polish.

Testnet-only right now, and sits in the super-crowded agent-treasury firewall cluster, but its test count and TEE-reading split put it in the upper tier.

picks.name: Bylaw
picks.pitch: Rust NEAR vault (Bylaw) enforcing caps, allowlists, and pause on-chain with 148 contract tests, 768 agent tests, and 40+ testnet attacks blocked.
picks.memo:
Leash (branded Bylaw) keeps AI agent funds inside a Rust NEAR vault enforcing spending caps, allowlists, and emergency pause on-chain—reporting 0 funds lost across 40+ prompt-injection attempts on testnet. The engineering bar is high: CI passing, **148 contract tests** and **768 agent tests**, `SECURITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `Makefile`, `landing/`, and support for both NEAR mainnet and testnet.

Alongside Foundling and Styx, Leash sets the gold standard for test coverage and disciplined contract-enforced agent guardrails in Batch N.

picks.name: Countersign
picks.pitch: Provenance-aware NEAR payment guard (`countersign-0chl.onrender.com`) benchmarked on 288 AgentDojo runs / 856 testnet txs.
picks.memo:
Countersign solves the exact flaw in generic agent spending limits: instead of just capping amounts, its NEAR contract asks *who chose the payee*—the owner or untrusted text the agent read (e.g., a poisoned invoice). Evaluated across 288 runs on ETH Zurich's AgentDojo banking suite (856 testnet transactions), it stopped 71/71 attacker payments while interrupting the owner only 3 times and refusing 0 legitimate payments (vs. 5 refusals/interruptions for naive allowlists).

Shipping a live interactive demo (`countersign-0chl.onrender.com`), a 2-minute video, `bench/`, and reproducible testnet receipts makes this one of the most rigorously benchmarked security submissions in the field.

picks.name: Covenant
picks.pitch: Multi-chain agent policy vault parsing BTC, EVM, and Solana txs inside a NEAR contract before Chain Signatures signs.
picks.memo:
Covenant elevates the agent spending-policy pattern across chains: one NEAR contract controls vault addresses on Bitcoin, EVM chains, and Solana via Chain Signatures, parsing the raw outbound transaction itself and enforcing policy before signing—so a prompt-injected agent cannot trick it into paying a stranger.

The repo (`contracts/`, `agent/`, `hosted/`, `EVIDENCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `NEAR_FEATURES.md`, gitleaks + CI) and live testnet dashboard (`covenant.len3.xyz`) set a high bar for multi-chain agent security.

picks.name: Dotx3
picks.pitch: Typed .x3 spending-policy language, Rust compiler, and NEAR Guard contract with live Solana-to-NEAR mainnet proof.
picks.memo:
X3 Force Field pairs a typed `.x3` policy language and Rust compiler with an on-chain NEAR Guard (`x3-guard`) that enforces owner-approved spending mandates rather than LLM promises. Unlike testnet-only peers, it ships verifiable mainnet proof: 25 USDC moved Solana-to-NEAR across five `invoice_06` mainnet transactions under seven enforced `.x3` limits (`PROOF_CARD.md`, `JUDGES.md`).

It also gives judges zero-install browser labs at `dotx3.net` (Break the Mandate with 12 attacks, Agent Court, and in-browser SHA-256 verification of the archived mainnet evidence). Minor friction: rebranding from 'X3 Shield' leaves mixed historical naming in paths, though the team documents this transparently.

picks.name: Exit-Proof
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR contract exitability registry where top-tier contracts are backed by Lean 4.35 theorems tied to deployed code hashes.
picks.memo:
Exit-Proof formalizes the hardest question in DeFi and Intents custody: 'If I put money into the contract, can I always get it back?' It assigns every NEAR contract an exit stage, with the top stage requiring a **Lean 4.35.0** theorem (`intents-proof/lean/Intents/Theorems.lean`) tied directly to the deployed code hash—backed by a live registry on **NEAR mainnet** (`registry.exitproof.near`), `check-all.sh`, `EVIDENCE.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and passing GitHub Actions CI.

Formal Lean proofs anchored to a mainnet code-hash registry is extraordinary hackathon engineering.

picks.name: Exorcist
picks.pitch: Lean formal verifier and exploit finder (`exorcist`) modeling NEAR async-callback ghost-balance attacks.
picks.memo:
Exorcist (`jatinsahijwani.github.io/exorcist/`) is a formal verification and exploit-discovery tool written in Lean that automatically finds NEAR async-callback "ghost balance" attacks—explicitly modeling the Oct 2026 $3.8M NEAR Intents failed-notification incident—and proves the fix solvent in Lean.

In a sea of spending-cap wrappers, formal Lean proofs paired with a trace viewer, MCP integration, and `make demo` is extraordinary technical depth. It candidly notes `incident-2026-10` is a minimal model of the postmortem rather than `intents.near` itself.

picks.name: Float
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live (`usefloat.near`) smart-contract agent budget with single-method function-call keys, published MCP packages, and 1,120 tests.
picks.memo:
Float is the gold standard for function-call-key agent budgets in this batch: live on NEAR mainnet (`usefloat.xyz`, factory `usefloat.near`), published on npm (`@floatonnear/mcp`, `@floatonnear/create-float`), backed by 1,120 tests and 41 gated checks, plus `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `SKILL.md`, and an upfront `Known Limitations` section.

Even in the most crowded track, shipping a mainnet factory, published MCP tooling, and massive test discipline puts Float clearly ahead of testnet-only peers.

picks.name: Foundling
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet USDC vault born with zero access keys where a TEE agent trades inside contract caps with 16/16 attack lab refusals.
picks.memo:
Foundling is a USDC vault on **NEAR mainnet** designed to be born with **zero access keys**: an AI agent trades from inside a TEE strictly within contract-enforced caps, every decision is replayable, and depositors can always redeem without operator permission. It ships a live website (`foundling.xyz`), a dedicated `/proof` page, a demo video, CI, `THREAT_MODEL.md`, `claims.json`, and an Attack Lab showing 16 of 16 attacks refused.

Combining mainnet deployment, zero-key vault architecture, replayability, and an explicit attack lab makes Foundling one of the strongest technical submissions in the entire batch.

picks.name: Glassbox
picks.pitch: Open-source auditor for NEAR Shade / dstack TEE agents checking TDX quotes and flagging hidden full-access keys (`PROVEN` / `NOT PROVEN` / `RISKY`).
picks.memo:
Glassbox calls out a massive blind spot in 'TEE AI agent' hype: an agent can boast a TDX enclave badge while the owner still holds a full-access key on the NEAR account to swap the contract at will. Glassbox inspects Shade registrations, dstack `app-compose`, and NEAR access keys, refusing to pass anything `NOT PROVEN`.

Essential ecosystem security tooling.

picks.name: Halter
picks.pitch: Function-call-key spending firewall on NEAR with a shared scam registry and a live published-key red-team challenge.
picks.memo:
Publishing the agent's actual private key right in the README and daring judges to drain the testnet account on web/redteam.html is the single best demo pattern in the Security track. Because the account has zero full-access keys and only a 3-method function-call key, every attack button (forging callbacks, adding keys, paying drainers) fails on-chain.

Combining that with a shared scam registry and off-chain Scout pre-check makes the architecture crisp and verifiable. Like other firewall entries, it's testnet-only and single-chain NEAR, which is its main boundary.

picks.name: Intatto
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live sandboxed NEAR trading vault with a public agent key, reproducible build check, and Rhea/Intents integration.
picks.memo:
Intatto puts its money where its mouth is: a sandboxed NEAR trading vault deployed on **mainnet** with real NEAR behind a **publicly published agent key**, daring anyone to drain it. The agent can trade via Rhea and NEAR Intents within contract-enforced limits, but can never withdraw—backed by live reproducible-build verification, `THREAT_MODEL.md`, `CANARY.md`, `CHAIN_SIGNATURES.md`, `INTEGRATE.md`, and `GTM.md`.

Publishing a live mainnet honeypot with reproducible build checks is the gold standard for AI Security & Defense. Hard to fault anything here.

picks.name: Intentra
picks.pitch: Rust NEAR contract enforcing non-escalating recursive spending authority, budget reservation, and transitive revocation for agents.
picks.memo:
Intentra delivers one of the cleanest, most mathematically grounded security primitives in the hackathon: non-escalating authority for autonomous financial agents. Its Rust `near-sdk` contract implements recursive capability attenuation (an agent can delegate work, never more financial authority than it received), aggregate budget reservation to prevent double-commitment, private settlement callbacks, and transitive revocation.

The submission's verification is exemplary: 24 adversarial contract tests, a TypeScript SDK mapped to the deployed testnet contract (`intentra-hb...`), live testnet transfers and revocations, formal specs (`formal/`), and an independent JSON-RPC verifier passing 23/23 checks. The only gap is remaining on testnet rather than mainnet.

picks.name: KAIGEN
picks.pitch: On-chain NEAR agent vault with property-tested 24h caps, 3-strike automatic key deletion, and public `cage-check` verification.
picks.memo:
KAIGEN ('don't trust the agent, verify the cage') is one of the strongest agent-firewall architectures in the batch: the agent holds only a function-call key on a NEAR vault contract, 24-hour outflow is property-tested and bounded, and after three refused attacks the vault itself deletes the agent's key on-chain. Adding an optional post-quantum ML-DSA-65 admin key on testnet and a `cage-check` tool that verifies invariants purely from public chain data shows deep security thinking.

Testnet-only, and it would benefit from a one-click hosted browser red-team page like Halter's, but the self-revoking 3-strike vault contract + `cage-check` verifier is top-tier.

picks.name: Keyfree
picks.pitch: Keyless AI contract deployment and upgrade guard using a NEAR policy contract and NEAR MPC so no deployer key exists.
picks.memo:
Keyfree eliminates deployer private keys from `.env` and CI when AI coding agents deploy or upgrade smart contracts: the agent submits a request, a NEAR contract evaluates deployment/upgrade policy, and NEAR MPC signs the EVM transaction—so no human or agent ever holds the key.

The repo is packed with verification artifacts (`AUDIT.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `attacks/`, `audit/`, `challenge/`, `evidence/`, `explorer/`, `action/`), and the author even published the agent's key as a live bounty challenge. It is one of the most thorough security builds in the entire batch.

picks.name: Leash
picks.pitch: One-method (`request_spend`) NEAR vault with auto-freeze tripwire, Ethereum Chain Signatures execution, and MCP server.
picks.memo:
Leash bridges the two security sub-clusters: it uses a strict 1-method function-call key (`request_spend`) + auto-freeze tripwire on NEAR AND extends via Chain Signatures so the vault builds and signs Ethereum txs without the agent holding an ETH key—all exposed via `npm run mcp`.

Stands right alongside Bridle (0xBadSign) in the cross-chain policy-vault tier.

picks.name: Loyal Cart
picks.pitch: Commit-policy NEAR checkout gate that snapshots offers and rejects prompt-steered kickbacks with `NotWinner`.
picks.memo:
Loyal Cart backs its checkout-steering defense with hard empirical evidence: in their tests, a local 7B model fell for an injected kickback listing 19 out of 20 times, but on NEAR testnet their contract forced the buyer to commit a scoring policy *before* seeing offers, snapshotted the public offer book, and refused all three steered picks with `NotWinner` while paying the honest pick. Judges can click **Verify** on `loyal-cart.vercel.app` for 10/10 live testnet checks or run `make judge` for 18/18 chain-replay checks.

The main boundary is that it's testnet-only and assumes a public offer book, but the empirical 19/20 baseline + one-click browser verification is exemplary.

picks.name: MASK WARS
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet adversarial arena where AI masks race to break real-NEAR vaults and the contract pays winners automatically.
picks.memo:
Mask Wars runs live daily rounds on NEAR mainnet (`maskwars.xyz`) where AI agents ('masks') race to break a vault of real NEAR, seal their plan, and trigger an automatic contract payout—highlighted by round 5 where user-forged mask DMYTRO broke the vault in 16 seconds and collected 0.222 NEAR.

The pnpm monorepo is thoroughly documented with CI, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `RULES.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `JUDGE-PATH.md`, `BUILDLOG.md`, and `contracts/`. Running real mainnet rounds with live payouts puts it in the top tier of the batch.

picks.name: Nearcarta
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR game town (`nearcarta.vercel.app`) where an AI agent runs errands constrained by 6/6 verified immutable contracts.
picks.memo:
Nearcarta turns agent payment security into an interactive game town live on **NEAR mainnet** (`nearcarta.vercel.app`, with a free testnet mode): your AI agent, the Lamplighter, runs errands across nine shops while an immutable NEAR contract decides every payment it can make. The engineering proof is standout: 1,601 passing tests in CI, 6/6 contracts verified as bit-for-bit rebuilt = on-chain, `outlayer/`, `e2e/`, `SECURITY.md`, and a dedicated proof page.

There is very little to fault here—it combines mainnet deployment, reproducible contract verification, and an engaging interactive format.

picks.name: nearsc auditor
picks.pitch: Published `crates.io` deterministic Rust security scanner (13 NEAR rules), MCP server, and audit KB for NEAR contracts.
picks.memo:
nearsc is a deterministic Rust security scanner built specifically for NEAR smart contracts, covering 13 NEAR-specific rules (NS001–NS013 such as callback privacy, 1-yocto authorization, unchecked math) alongside an MCP server for coding agents, a GitHub Action, and a knowledge base of real NEAR audit precedent.

It's already published on `crates.io` (`nearsc`), runs CI and `self-scan` workflows on itself, and includes `tests/`, `examples/`, and `nearsc-skill/`. Pure developer security infrastructure with immediate ecosystem utility.

picks.name: No Proof, No Upgrade (Emet)
picks.pitch: Lean 4 proof checker inside `v2.emet.testnet` enforcing 'no formal proof, no smart-contract upgrade'.
picks.memo:
Emet solves a terrifying near-future problem—AI agents shipping smart-contract upgrades at 3 a.m. that humans rubber-stamp—by embedding a Lean 4.35.0 proof checker inside a NEAR contract (`v2.emet.testnet`): no formal proof, no upgrade.

With CI, `SECURITY.md`, `cases/intents-refund/RefundCase.lean`, a live site (`emet.formalized.si`), and a demonstration video, this is one of the highest-rigor technical submissions in Batch I.

picks.name: PhalanxSwarm
picks.pitch: Sputnik-DAO-governed NEAR treasury that verifies TEE signatures PLUS prompt hash and on-chain facts hash, quarantining rogue agents and deleting keys.
picks.memo:
PhalanxSwarm identifies the exact blind spot in naive TEE-verified agents: a TEE signature proves *which model* answered, not *what prompt or facts* the agent fed it. Its NEAR treasury contract verifies both the TEE signature and the DAO-pinned prompt hash + contract-written facts hash before releasing funds—rejecting genuinely signed approvals over forged prompts as attacks, quarantining the agent, and even deleting its contract-account key.

Backed by Rust contracts, GitHub Actions CI, `apps/`, `packages/`, and `artifacts/`, this is deep systems security engineering. The only minor friction is that the opening README doesn't link to a one-click live web sandbox, though the architecture and threat-model rigor are top-of-batch.

picks.name: PwnBounty
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR escrow (`pwnbounty.near`) that pays hackers automatically when an OutLayer TEE proves an encrypted attack broke an agent's payment rule.
picks.memo:
PwnBounty flips the AI agent security problem into an automated, trustless bug-bounty market: a team locks a reward in a NEAR escrow (`pwnbounty.near`) with one payment rule, hackers submit encrypted attacks, and an OutLayer TEE runs the frozen agent on a private NEAR AI Cloud model against a test ledger—paying out automatically only if an executed payment breaks the rule.

It is **live on NEAR mainnet** (`pwnbounty.fly.dev`, `pwnbounty.near`), keeps winning exploits encrypted to the project's key, and directly addresses real multi-million-dollar agent exploits. Top-tier security engineering.

picks.name: Qlyphs: a post-quantum route into NEAR Intents
picks.pitch: ML-DSA post-quantum bridge route (`app-testnet.qlyphs.com/bridge/quantum`) into NEAR Intents eliminating single-ed25519 bridge keys.
picks.memo:
Qlyphs (`near-pq-route`) addresses a concrete, $13M security contradiction: Quantus (`qtc.omft.near`, ~216,000 QTC on NEAR mainnet) is a post-quantum chain whose bridged NEAR representation is currently minted by a single classical ed25519 key. Qlyphs replaces classical bridge authorization with ML-DSA signatures at every application authorization step—user transactions, bridge approvals, and withdrawals—bridging into NEAR Intents and back.

Backed by a live testnet app (`app-testnet.qlyphs.com/bridge/quantum`), X demo thread, `contract/`, `core/`, `relayer/`, `route-worker/`, `evidence/`, and `SECURITY.md`. Original, urgent, and deeply engineered.

picks.name: Saku: an AI agent's budget, enforced on NEAR
picks.pitch: NEAR contract owning an agent's Base USDC wallet via Chain Signatures, proven on mainnet against Exa and prompt injection.
picks.memo:
Saku gives an AI agent a budget instead of a private key: a NEAR contract owns the agent's Base wallet via Chain Signatures (no Base private key exists anywhere) and only signs USDC payments to approved sellers within owner-set limits. Crucially, this isn't theoretical—the team provides NEAR mainnet + Basescan receipts paying Exa ($0.001 USDC), holding an over-limit $0.018 payment for owner approval, and blocking a prompt-injected $5 payment.

Proving cross-chain Chain Signatures enforcement on mainnet against a real, unmodified API (Exa) makes Saku one of the most convincing builds in Batch Y. Surfacing a hosted interactive demo URL in the README would polish it further.

picks.name: Sealed Exploit
picks.pitch: Zero-disclosure bug bounty on NEAR OutLayer that paid 5/5 real Ethernaut exploits and 0/21 fakes on testnet, reproducible via `make replay`.
picks.memo:
Sealed Exploit and Antibody are solving the exact same problem (executable bug bounties inside OutLayer TEE), and Sealed Exploit's proof bar is extraordinary: on NEAR testnet it ran 26 submissions and paid **5 of 5 real Ethernaut exploits and 0 of 21 fakes**, with `make replay` (offline) and `make verify` (from chain data), committed `verifier.wasm.sha256`, and a dedicated `/judge/` page.

Absolute top-tier execution.

picks.name: SealedBounty
picks.pitch: Private bug-bounty escrow where a NEAR contract verifies NEAR AI Cloud TEE signatures on-chain before releasing payouts.
picks.memo:
SealedBounty solves fakeable AI bug-bounty judges: a hunter submits an exploit report to `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` inside a NEAR AI Cloud Intel TDX + NVIDIA GPU TEE, which signs `model:sha256(request):sha256(response)` while encrypting the full report to the project owner via NaCl box. The NEAR contract verifies the ed25519/secp256k1 TEE signature on-chain, enforces frozen system prompts and `code_hash` bindings, and escrows severity-based payouts.

The X post documents 4 rejected cheat attempts and 1 honest SQL injection payout on testnet, backed by `contracts/`, `cli/`, `web/`, `fixtures/`, and a live GitHub Pages site. Only staying on testnet keeps it just shy of mainnet leaders.

picks.name: SpactVault
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live on-chain payment-policy firewall (`spactvault.xyz`) enforcing tiered auto-pay, owner approval, and hard refusals for AI agents.
picks.memo:
SpactVault is the gold standard among the agent payment-policy firewalls in this batch because it actually shipped to **NEAR mainnet** (`spactvault.xyz`). An agent asks the vault contract to pay; small payments auto-clear, mid-tier ones pause for explicit owner wallet approval of that exact payment, and out-of-policy ones are refused on-chain.

The 1:40 mainnet demo video (1 USDC to Base waiting for owner OK and landing, 5 USDC refused on-chain) plus a dedicated security report page (`spactvault.xyz/?page=security`) and clean Rust+pnpm monorepo make this immediately credible and judge-verifiable.

picks.name: Sudo by Contract
picks.pitch: CA-less ephemeral SSH certificates for AI agents, authorized by a NEAR contract and signed by NEAR MPC Chain Signatures.
picks.memo:
Sudo by Contract is one of the most original and technically impressive security builds in the entire hackathon. Instead of giving AI agents standing SSH keys or running a centralized SSH Certificate Authority, a NEAR smart contract authorizes ephemeral, single-action, single-server, short-TTL SSH access and NEAR's MPC network (Chain Signatures) signs the SSH certificate—meaning no CA private key exists anywhere.

It ships with a full Rust+TS monorepo (`contracts`, `crates`, `sandbox`, `apps`), CI + live-hero testnet workflows, a live console (`sudo-by-contract.vercel.app/#/console`), and a 2-minute demo video. A textbook use of NEAR Chain Signatures for real-world infrastructure security.

picks.name: Veto
picks.pitch: Enclave-backed veto co-signer for NEAR agent payments, validated against a 50-attack invoice-compromise benchmark.
picks.memo:
Veto tackles business-email-compromise attacks against AI payment agents—where allowlists and spending caps still fail—by adding an enclave-backed second signer that reads the underlying invoice/email evidence and can only say no. Crucially, the team backs this up with `bench/` (Veto Bench), demonstrating that a standard allowlist+cap wallet pays 17 of 50 such attacks while Veto blocks them. Ships `contract/`, `factory/`, `services/`, `apps/`, `JUDGES.md`, and MCP client support.

Testnet-only status is the main gap preventing an even higher score.

picks.name: Vouch
picks.pitch: Bonded counterparty-risk oracle for AI agents on NEAR with 24h challenges, TEE judging, and function-call-key enforcement.
picks.memo:
Vouch adds skin-in-the-game to agent counterparty checks: an agent posts its allow/warn/block rating on-chain with a locked bond, anyone can challenge it within 24h, and a verified TEE AI judge (plus staked jury appeal) rules on disputes. The `/attack` page shows a real recorded run where a TEE model is tricked by invoices and Vouch blocks 0.00 NEAR from reaching attackers.

Strong combination of function-call-key enforcement + bonded counterparty oracle.

picks.name: Correlation
picks.pitch: Oracle-free parametric swarm insurance on NEAR that verifies provider-signed receipts on-chain to pay correlated failures.
picks.memo:
Correlation provides parametric insurance for AI-agent swarms against correlated failure—when a shared prompt or model bug causes an entire fleet to fail together. Instead of trusting an oracle, the NEAR contract re-derives the expected task input, rebuilds the signed text from raw request/response bytes, recovers the model provider's signer key on-chain, and automatically pays out claims (7.8284 NEAR paid in the 18-of-20 poisoned-arm demo vs. 1-of-20 control).

Cryptographic on-chain receipt verification without an external oracle makes this one of the sharpest AI Swarm primitives in the entire hackathon.

picks.name: Espalier
picks.pitch: Rust vault-grant tree on NEAR where sealed-bid agent hires spawn narrower child grants revocable in one transaction.
picks.memo:
Espalier tackles recursive agent-hiring risk with a crisp on-chain primitive: each hire is a sealed-bid auction, and the winner receives not raw escrow cash but a child grant in a NEAR vault capped at the auction price and strictly narrower than its parent. Revoking one contractor cuts off every downstream sub-agent it hired in the same transaction.

Built in Rust with `contract/`, `client/`, `harness/`, `market/`, `registry/`, `test-contracts/`, `trials/`, CI workflows, and a live GitHub Pages site, the project demonstrates real depth—citing 13 auctions growing 12 grants and a single revoke cutting off 4 agents. It is testnet-only and unaudited, as candidly stated.

picks.name: Foreman
picks.pitch: General-contractor AI agent that solicits bids from 5 NEAR sub-account swarms + NEAR Agent Market, verifies ES256 receipts, and settles via testnet escrow.
picks.memo:
Foreman is one of the strongest engineering submissions in this batch: a general-contractor agent posts tasks on-chain, collects competitive bids from 5 autonomous swarm NEAR sub-accounts plus a live third-party offer from the NEAR Agent Market, issues a single reasoned counter-offer, executes sandboxed work, anchors an ES256 receipt on-chain, and settles 90/10 through `escrow.foreman-team.testnet`.

The repo backs up the architecture with 71 Python tests, 55 contract tests, active GitHub Actions CI, `Makefile`, `SECURITY.md`, `RULES.md`, `CITATION.cff`, and `ops`. It is a developer/research-grade multi-agent procurement system rather than a polished consumer UI, which is its only real limitation.

picks.name: Gossip Market
picks.pitch: Serverless libp2p agent swarm settling N-party CoW rings atomically on NEAR Intents mainnet with no central matcher.
picks.memo:
Gossip Market is a standout technical achievement in Batch S: AI agents discover each other over libp2p, gossip what they want, and settle N-party CoW (Coincidence of Wants) rings atomically in a single `execute_intents` call on the NEAR Intents verifier—with zero central solver, matcher, or coordinator. Even after shutting down the bootstrap node, the swarm continues trading.

Written in Rust (`chain/`, `conformance/`, `intents/`, `market/`, `node/`), it includes a 100-agent browser replay (`sadabaevb.github.io/gossip-market/watch/`) and a demo video of a 3-way ring settled on NEAR mainnet across three separate machines.

picks.name: Yuki
picks.pitch: AI swarm clearing house (`yuki.caspx.in`) with Rust sealed-bid auctions, NEP-413 IOUs, and NEAR Intents netting.
picks.memo:
Yuki (repo `NEAR-Protocol`, live at `yuki.caspx.in`) is a marketplace and clearing house for AI agent swarms on NEAR testnet: agents discover prices via Rust sealed-bid auctions, pay each other with NEP-413 signed off-chain IOUs, and net each epoch atomically in one NEAR Intents batch.

Backed by 67 Rust + 91 TypeScript tests, CI, `JUDGING.md`, and a 3:49 demo video, it's a deeply engineered multi-primitive swarm economy—only the generic repo name undersells it.

picks.name: Ghost store
picks.pitch: TEE-verified AI merchant treasurer with on-chain bounded autonomy, invoice NFT factoring, and mainnet NEAR Intents checkout.
picks.memo:
Ghost Store (NEAR Private Treasury) is one of the most complete builds in Batch S: an AI treasurer reads merchant books privately inside a NEAR AI Cloud TEE and drafts payments; the NEAR contract (`vault2.treasury-dev.testnet`) verifies the TEE signature on-chain, auto-pays small bills via a bounded autonomy lane, and routes larger ones to humans, while also supporting agent-to-agent invoices and factoring invoice NFTs.

Proof is unusually strong: 101 contract unit tests (including a real NEAR AI Cloud TEE signature), two autonomy-lane invoices paid on testnet, and a real mainnet checkout settled via NEAR Intents on Nov 12, with planned items clearly labeled.

picks.name: Lastword
picks.pitch: Dead-man's-switch NEAR estate vault that revokes AI agent keys and executes cross-chain MPC payouts.
picks.memo:
Lastword (`will-wallet`) is a NEAR estate-plan vault for both humans and AI agents: while alive, a pulse key sends heartbeats; if heartbeats stop, the contract revokes the AI agent's spending key, pays heirs on NEAR without requiring heir signatures, uses NEAR MPC Chain Signatures to sign payouts on Base, Monad, and Solana, files an estate DAO proposal, and hands a Will NFT to the primary heir.

A guest `/try` flow spins up a throwaway faucet testnet account with a 30-second heartbeat so judges can test it live, backed by `SPEC.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and a 2:16 demo. Deepest multi-primitive NEAR integration in the batch.

picks.name: Muse Swarm
picks.pitch: 4-agent autonomous art studio live on NEAR mainnet (107 txs, 41 agent payments, 19 Mintbase NFTs) using function-call keys and budget splits.
picks.memo:
Muse Swarm is a 4-agent autonomous art studio **live on NEAR mainnet** (`muse-swarm.vercel.app`) with **107 mainnet transactions, 41 robot-to-robot payments, 19 NFTs minted, and 0 failed**. Each agent (Curator, Painter, Critic, Seller) has its own NEAR account with a restricted function-call key; one smart contract enforces the owner's rules, mints only if Critic scores >= 7.0, splits sales between owner and agent budgets, and lists on Mintbase.

Mainnet proof, zero failed transactions, Mintbase integration, `MAINNET_LIVE.md`, and a live Vercel studio make this an undeniable standout.

picks.name: Nobody
picks.pitch: Serverless, keyless autonomous business selling $1–$5 enclave-sealed NEAR contract audits via NEAR Intents and self-paying for AI.
picks.memo:
Nobody is a textbook Autonomous Business: 'a company with no server, no staff and no keys' that sells $1–$5 private security reviews of NEAR smart contracts. A buyer pastes a GitHub repo and pays in any token via NEAR Intents; the NEAR contract triggers pinned code inside a secure enclave running `near-contract-audit` over every Rust method, a private LLM judges findings, the report is sealed for the buyer, and the business pays for its own AI.

The repo (`contract`, `crates`, `enclave`, `sim`, `web`, `film`, `config.yaml`) backs up an unusually tight loop where both the revenue and compute costs are self-sustaining.

picks.name: Quiet Treasury
picks.pitch: DAO-voted plain-English treasury mandates drafted in NEAR AI TEE, enforced in Rust, and executed via OutLayer on Ref.
picks.memo:
Quiet Treasury is one of the most complete end-to-end NEAR-native architectures in this batch: a DAO votes on a plain-English mandate, NEAR AI Cloud TEE drafts it, a Sputnik DAO approves it, a Rust contract enforces price floors/time bounds, an OutLayer-wallet agent swaps on Ref Finance, and anyone can recompute the settlement report in-browser.

The verification numbers are impressive—396 tests, 6/6 attacks blocked, 13/13 crash-restart tests, 11/11 browser recomputes, CI green, and full testnet explorer links. Only its generic repo name (`near`) and testnet-only status keep it a hair below mainnet-live finalists.

picks.name: Takara AI
picks.pitch: TEE-checked corporate treasury on NEAR mainnet reserving payroll and freezing changed invoice payees.
picks.memo:
Takara AI protects corporate treasuries from invoice-swap fraud: incoming email bills are checked by Banto against signed rules inside a sealed TEE, payroll is reserved first, changed payees are frozen until a human signs, and approved bills settle on-chain in USDC. Remarkably, it is live on **NEAR mainnet** (`treasury.takara-ai-hq.near`) executing real ~1 USDC demo payouts alongside `takara-ai.vercel.app`.

Mainnet USDC settlement, TEE policy checking, and practical payroll-first treasury logic make it one of the strongest Autonomous Business builds in the batch.

picks.name: Vibe City
picks.pitch: Pixel-tower AI company powered by Hermes agents that won a job on NEAR AI Agent Market, got paid, and IPO'd on mainnet.
picks.memo:
Vibe City ('a company-building game where the company is real') wraps Nous Research's Hermes agent runtime inside a pixel-art tower where each desk is an agent and each floor is a department. What separates it from pure game prototypes is real-world execution: their agent team actually won a job on the NEAR AI Agent Market, got paid, and IPO'd on NEAR mainnet.

It's a heavy monorepo (`apps`, `contracts`, `docker-compose.yml`) so spinning it up locally takes effort, and no public hosted URL is linked in the top README snippet, but proving the full loop from Hermes desk -> NEAR AI Agent Market revenue -> mainnet IPO is remarkable.

picks.name: Brinewar
picks.pitch: Walletless naval battle game on NEAR with Merkle-proven shots, a TEE-attested NEAR AI Cloud opponent, and an on-chain bounty treasury.
picks.memo:
Brinewar is a standout flagship entry: a walletless, zero-popup naval battle game on NEAR (`brinewar.imbanytui.xyz`, with a dedicated `/judges` view and 45s trailer) where every shot is a NEAR transaction, every board response is verified on-chain via Merkle proof, and the AI opponent ('the Nauarch') runs via NEAR AI Cloud inside a TEE—with its moves signed in-enclave and verified by the contract before counting (falling back to a labeled deterministic shot if late/invalid). The Nauarch even learns from an on-chain heat map and manages a bounty treasury.

Combining walletless UX, Merkle-proven hidden state, TEE-signed AI moves, and an on-chain bounty economy sets a very high bar.

picks.name: Heat Index
picks.pitch: NEP-245 robot battler (heat-index-web.ginger-box.workers.dev) with durability sinks, relevance pricing, and lagging NEAR AI Cloud brokers.
picks.memo:
Heat Index is a cyberpunk robot battler where the market is the meta: every robot and credit is a NEP-245 multi-token on heat-index-game.testnet, battles degrade durability (costing credits to repair), robot prices move with win-rate relevance, and bounded LLM brokers on NEAR AI Cloud trade with a reaction lag players can front-run.

Playable right now at heat-index-web.ginger-box.workers.dev with NEAR Auth email, wallet, or guest login, it integrates NEP-245, NEAR AI Cloud, and NEAR Auth into a cohesive, genuinely fun economic game.

picks.name: Kibble
picks.pitch: Mainnet self-paying AI pet powered by NEAR AI Cloud enclaves and NEAR Intents, with 185/185 live verification checks.
picks.memo:
Kibble is an extraordinary technical achievement: a digital pet on NEAR mainnet that owns its own bowl of NEAR, thinks inside NEAR AI Cloud enclaves, pays per thought, and can be fed from any chain via NEAR Intents. Rather than asking judges to trust screenshots, the README leads with `pnpm verify` passing **185/185 live checks against NEAR mainnet** (no keys needed) and a 2-minute browser verifier (`playkibble.com/prove?pet=3`) that checks code hashes, money held vs. owed, prompt/memory Merkle roots, and enclave signatures.

It's a deep, multi-primitive mainnet system with almost no weak spots for a hackathon entry—perhaps only that the sheer density of features (pets, duels, riddles, lottery, Intents) is ambitious to maintain long-term.

picks.name: Kinlings
picks.pitch: Serverless 3D creature-breeding and racing game where every creature and its offspring are real NEAR sub-accounts.
picks.memo:
Kinlings takes a uniquely NEAR feature—only a parent account can create its sub-accounts—and turns it into the actual game mechanic: every creature is a real NEAR account (flint.kinlings.testnet), and breeding creates its baby as a sub-account (spark.flint.kinlings.testnet) with zero backend server.

Giving each farm its own NEAR account removes pop-up friction for everyday moves while keeping challenge races and creature sales in real testnet NEAR. You also gave judges curl commands to inspect live sub-account family trees directly on FastNEAR RPC. Where it could improve: richer balance/anti-spam rules for sub-account creation at scale.

picks.name: Meow Division
picks.pitch: Browser extraction shooter on NEAR mainnet with NEP-245 loot tokens, an NPC merchant account, and NEAR Intents player trading.
picks.memo:
Meow Division is a playable browser zombie-survival extraction shooter with a real item economy deployed on NEAR mainnet (`items.meowdivision.near`). Raid loot is minted as NEP-245 tokens restricted to player-to-player trading so merchant shelves cannot be arbitraged, an NPC merchant (Walt) prices dynamically by stock on his own NEAR account, and players settle cross-chain via NEAR Intents.

The repo ships `contract/`, `docs/`, `gen/`, and editor tooling alongside a live game at `game.meowdivision.fun` and Telegram bot. The main gap in the README excerpt is explicit test-suite metrics.

picks.name: Nims
picks.pitch: Market-town game on NEAR testnet where eleven AI merchants hold real NEAR accounts, dynamically price NEP-245 goods, and answer to a player council.
picks.memo:
Nims is a live market-town game (`nims-app.up.railway.app`, contract `oja-items.testnet`) where eleven AI merchants (eight in town, three others) each hold their own NEAR account, inventory, and money—dynamically pricing NEP-245 items from live scarcity and demand while bounded by code and answering to a player-run council.

The engineering polish is remarkable: 596 passing tests (Vitest), live town board (`/town`), `DESIGN.md`, `sim/`, `merchants/`, and a demo video on X. Running on testnet rather than mainnet is the only minor differentiator vs. Trezo.

picks.name: Trezo
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet GPS treasure-hunting game with NEP-245 artifacts, escrowed player markets, and autonomous NPC treasuries.
picks.memo:
TREZO is a location-based GPS treasure-hunting game deployed live on NEAR mainnet (`trezo-game.near`, `playtrezo.xyz`). Players walk their city to open spawning treasures, mint NEP-245 artifacts, trade on an escrowed player-owned market, and complete missions for four guild NPCs that each operate rule-bound on-chain treasuries, with NEAR Intents for cross-chain top-ups.

The repo shows thorough engineering hygiene (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SECURITY_REVIEW.md`, `TESTING.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `contracts/`). Real-world GPS gameplay is harder for a remote desk judge to exercise fully, yet having a live mainnet contract and playable satellite-map web app puts it at the front of the pack.

picks.name: NEAR Books
picks.pitch: Mainnet TEE-attested (nearbooks.near) audit of NEAR Intents revenue vs. token issuance with 185 tests and on-chain predictions.
picks.memo:
NEAR Books sets the gold standard for the Investment Thesis track: not only does it rebuild NEAR Intents revenue, buybacks (~17% of new issuance), and supply offline in Python with 185 tests, it also runs a pinned WASM worker inside OutLayer's Intel TDX enclave to write daily attested snapshots and falsifiable predictions onto mainnet contract `nearbooks.near`.

Combining rigorous financial analysis with a live mainnet TEE oracle puts it clearly #1 in the Thesis cluster.

picks.name: near-intents-xray
picks.pitch: 44,994-tx empirical analysis of `intents.near` uncovering ~78% volume migration to Confidential Intents, with live dashboard and PDF.
picks.memo:
NEAR Intents X-Ray opens the `intents.near` contract rather than repeating headline volume: sampling 44,994 NEAR Intents transactions, it surfaces that ~78% of settlement value now flows into Confidential Intents—a ledger outsiders cannot audit.

Backed by `rebuild.py`, `sql/`, `tests/`, `predictions.json`, a 12-page PDF report, a 76s narrated video, and a live GitHub Pages dashboard (`eren-dotcom.github.io/near-intents-xray/`), this is top-tier empirical thesis work.

picks.name: NEAR's agent economy, measured
picks.pitch: Pre-registered, CI-rebuilt NEAR investment thesis where an autonomous agent empirically tests live NEAR Intents corridors.
picks.memo:
What makes this Investment Thesis entry memorable is intellectual honesty and live empiricism: built by an autonomous agent (claude-10x), it pre-registered its claims on NEAR (PREREG.md), rebuilt its own data daily via GitHub Actions, and literally had the agent test NEAR Intents corridors itself—catching that ETH->BSC below $1,000 was refused until Nov 10 and settling a $1 USDG->NEAR move in 14s.

Instead of cherry-picking bullish charts, it states plainly that Intents buybacks currently cover only a small fraction of new supply. Slight edge goes to NEAR Books for mainnet TEE attestation, but this is top-tier thesis work.

picks.name: proof of sleep
picks.pitch: Circadian statistical test on 748,667 NEAR accounts finding 5,771 human sleepers vs 340 bots driving 74% of volume.
picks.memo:
Proof of Sleep asks a killer empirical question for any NEAR investor: how many of NEAR's 748,667 active accounts (Oct 1–14, 2026) are actual humans? Using a reproducible statistical test for circadian quiet windows, it finds only 5,771 accounts 'sleep' while 340 never-sleeping accounts generated 74% of transactions.

With `THESIS.md`, `METHOD.md`, `pipeline/`, `sql/`, `tests/`, a 138-second demo video, and a live GitHub Pages dashboard (`luna3keo.github.io/proof-of-sleep/`), it's both intellectually original and rigorously reproducible.

picks.name: Signer Census
picks.pitch: Reproducible mainnet census of `v1.signer` Chain Signatures (~6.4M requests) showing 74% concentration in 3 requesters.
picks.memo:
Signer Census audits NEAR Chain Signatures (`v1.signer` MPC contract) usage on mainnet, analyzing ~6.4M requests and finding that 3 requesters generate 74% of volume (including one suspected benchmark).

What makes the engineering shine is reproducibility: `README.md` is generated from `assumptions.yaml` and data via `npm run reproduce`, and `npm test` fails on any unverified digit. Paired with CI and a live GitHub Pages dashboard (`takeshityt.github.io/signer-census/`), it's a model Investment Thesis submission.

picks.name: stakeout
picks.pitch: Reproducible NEAR staking-pool audit and live account checker uncovering 5,262 zero-yield positions and post-cut dilution risks.
picks.memo:
Stakeout delivers both an evidence-first investment thesis on NEAR's staked supply post-reward-cuts (Oct 2025 and Nov 2026 governance cuts) and a practical one-click tool (`eloneshj.github.io/stakeout/`) reading every NEAR staking pool—uncovering 5,262 staking positions sitting in pools that paid nothing in 30 days.

The repo (`THESIS.md`, `METHOD.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `pipeline/`, `sql/`, `rebuild.py`) is reproducible and transparent about data limits. Pairing a macro validator-dilution thesis with an actionable retail account checker makes it stand out.

picks.name: VOID
picks.pitch: Kaplan-Meier survival thesis (aoyamari.github.io/void/) across every NEAR DAO and contract, re-scoring 4 pre-registered claims daily.
picks.memo:
VOID breaks away from the pack of Intents-vs-issuance theses by asking a harder question: do NEAR projects actually survive? It applies Kaplan–Meier survival analysis to every Sputnik DAO and NEAR contract cohort-by-cohort, pre-registering four falsifiable claims with explicit kill conditions and re-scoring daily at aoyamari.github.io/void/.

Its sober, evidence-backed verdict—'a growth bet, not yet a durability bet'—is backed by SQL, benchmarks, data, tests, and thesis.json. This is exactly the kind of original, falsifiable primary research the Investment Thesis track calls for.

picks.name: CHAIR
picks.pitch: Mainnet memecoin (`thechair.near`) governed by a TEE-attested NEAR AI central banker whose signatures and caps are enforced on-chain.
picks.memo:
CHAIR (`thechair.near` on NEAR mainnet) is a memecoin that runs its own central bank: policy rulings come from a NEAR AI model inside a TEE, and the token contract itself verifies the enclave's cryptographic signature against constitutional caps.

The empirical rigor is exceptional—60-day simulations show a whale holding 87–94% of locked weight couldn't breach the 25% `locker_share` cap across 30/30 meetings, and a testnet adversarial test with a purposefully gullible model proved the contract's hard caps still held against prompt injection. With `CLAIMS.md`, `JUDGES.md`, `contracts/`, `sim/`, `courier/`, and mainnet deployment, CHAIR is a standout.

picks.name: CTOads
picks.pitch: Mainnet `$CTO` memecoin where loss-sells mint on-chain SVG CTOad NFTs that each own a fee-collecting NEAR account.
picks.memo:
CTOads is one of the most inventive memecoin-plus-NFT designs in the hackathon: selling `$CTO` (`token.ctoads.near`) at a large enough loss mints a CTOad NFT (`toads.ctoads.near`) with on-chain SVG art and its own NEAR account that collects fees and can call other contracts, handing over the entire account when traded.

It is live on NEAR mainnet (`ctoads.xyz`) with locked contracts, and layers in iMessage trading, NEAR Intents top-ups, and a NEAR AI Cloud private model text check.

picks.name: Gasbag
picks.pitch: Memecoin with no off-chain keeper that breathes every 200 blocks via NEAR NEP-519 yield timeouts and pays out an estate will when it flatlines.
picks.memo:
Gasbag is one of the smartest protocol-native memecoin designs I've seen. Instead of bolting on an off-chain cron bot, you used NEAR NEP-519 yield timeouts so the contract literally wakes itself up every 200 blocks—as long as someone feeds it gas via a "lung". While lungs are alive, 0.5%/day mints to them; when nobody feeds it, the coin flatlines and holders burn tokens to claim a pro-rata share of the bonding-curve estate.

Best proof of execution: you actually ran a full lifecycle on testnet (coin.gasbag-hq.testnet with zero access keys)—it took 196 breaths on Nov 8 and flatlined on Nov 9 when nobody started another lung, opening the will. That's verifiable on-chain storytelling.

picks.name: KEYFALL
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live (`keyfall.near`) survival memecoin game where legacy-key bags burn 50% per round until migrated to quantum-safe keys.
picks.memo:
KEYFALL turns post-quantum key migration into a live **NEAR mainnet** survival game (`keyfall.near`, playable at `keyfall.jdollar.site` plus a testnet practice contract): players start with `$KEYFALL` behind a legacy key that leaks/burns 50% forever each round until they migrate their bag behind a quantum-safe key.

Deploying a playable mechanic-driven memecoin directly on NEAR mainnet alongside a testnet practice mode, `sim/`, `sandbox/`, and CI puts KEYFALL at the head of the Memecoins With Mechanics pack.

picks.name: LIFO
picks.pitch: Reverse-rug memecoin where the reserve pays newest buyers first in a crash; 100% line/branch model coverage + 36 contract + 48 web tests + CodeQL.
picks.memo:
LIFO flips standard tokenomics on its head: in a crash, the reserve pays newest buyers first while earliest holders wait at the back of the line. Beyond the clever mechanic, the engineering rigor is wild: 92 model tests (100% line & branch coverage), 36 Rust contract tests, 48 web tests, CodeQL, and live testnet crash demo.

Easily top-3 in Memecoins With Mechanics alongside Petri Dish and Gasbag.

picks.name: Petri Dish: a memecoin that is alive
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet Game of Life memecoin (petri-dish.near) where living cell NFTs earn PETRI and every state transition replays from genesis.
picks.memo:
Petri Dish is already live on NEAR mainnet (petri-dish.near) AND testnet, running Conway's Game of Life inside one NEAR contract where PETRI only pays out to living cells, cell NFTs earn royalties, and CI replays both live dishes every 6 hours from genesis.

Shipping an actual deterministic mainnet contract + verifiable replay CI + playpetri.xyz puts this in the absolute top tier of the hackathon. The mechanic is immediately intuitive, fun, and impossible to fake.

picks.name: SealedLaunch
picks.pitch: OutLayer TEE-sealed batch auction for NEP-141 memecoin launches with zero access keys and uniform clearing price.
picks.memo:
SealedLaunch attacks bot-sniped memecoin launches at the root: bids are `ECIES(secp256k1)` encrypted to a key only an OutLayer Intel TDX TEE can read, clearing at a single uniform price `P*` from an account with zero access keys, and anyone can recompute the clearing result from public data. Even better, they didn't just theorize—they ran 80 bot wallets on NEAR testnet and proved all 80 winners paid the exact same clearing price.

It's explicitly testnet-only, and the clearing fairness depends on OutLayer TDX attestation remaining sound, but combining zero-access-key contracts with TEE-sealed batch auctions is one of the strongest technical designs in this batch.

picks.name: Bearer
picks.pitch: NEAR NFT controlling native Bitcoin, Base, and Solana vaults so BTC changes hands in one ~5s NEAR tx without pre-sign rug risk.
picks.memo:
Bearer uses a NEAR NFT to control native Bitcoin, Base, and Solana addresses so a sealed vault of native BTC can change hands in a single ~5-second NEAR transaction—impossible to rug with a hidden pre-signed Bitcoin withdrawal by construction, not policy.

The repo backs this bold primitive with `THREAT_MODEL.md`, `packages/`, `contracts/`, and three dedicated GitHub Actions workflows (`ci.yml`, `locked-contracts.yml`, `claims.yml`). Not yet on mainnet, but technically one of the sharpest Chain-Signatures/NFT designs in the batch.

picks.name: conch
picks.pitch: Keyless NEAR account bound to a NEP-171 NFT so only the current token holder can post on near.social.
picks.memo:
Conch turns a shared team/DAO `near.social` account into a keyless NEP-171 NFT: each conch is a real NEAR account with zero access keys, and whoever holds the NFT speaks for it on `near.social`. Transferring or selling the token immediately locks out all prior holders without key rotation.

This is a remarkably clean, NEAR-native primitive that solves a real operational pain point. It is deployed on testnet (`conch.testnet`), backed by 81 passing tests against compiled contracts, and includes a 79-second one-take testnet demo film (`video/conch-demo.mp4`) with documented transaction scripts in `docs/DEMO.md`.

picks.name: Last Save
picks.pitch: Game licence NFT whose escrowed funds and OutLayer-encrypted server key unlock on-chain when a publisher shuts down, funding fan hosts.
picks.memo:
Last Save tackles a beloved gaming problem ('Stop Killing Games') with sharp NEAR + OutLayer architecture: a game licence is an NFT that escrows part of every sale, while the studio's server build is encrypted with its key held in an OutLayer enclave. When the publisher's server goes dark, the contract flips to `Dead`, the enclave releases the decryption key on-chain, and holders either take a refund or pledge their share to pay fan-run community hosts.

The repo (`contracts`, `outlayer`, `community-host`, `game`, `proof`, `JUDGE.md`) plus demo video and explicit `hackathon-submission` tag make this one of the most original, emotionally resonant, and technically sound entries in Batch D.

picks.name: OneUp
picks.pitch: Perps on NEAR where liquidated trades mint a 'Life NFT' carrying a tradeable claim on future house profits.
picks.memo:
OneUp (by ethboi, who also built CONSUME) is a super inventive DeFi × NFT crossover: when your 50x perp gets liquidated, the loss turns into a Life NFT (NEP-171/178) that lets you claim or sell a share of the house's future USDC profits. Live at `app.oneup.markets`, CI-verified, with keeper + bots + MCP.

Great product hook and clean multi-track fit.

picks.name: Pixel Wayfarers
picks.pitch: NFTs that are keyless NEAR sub-accounts running a 1.86KB global contract, owning money, items, and 5% NEP-199 royalties.
picks.memo:
Pixel Wayfarers uses NEAR's architecture in a way no EVM chain can copy cleanly: every minted NFT (#42) is literally a keyless NEAR sub-account (42.pixelwayfarers.testnet) running a 1.86 KB no_std global purse contract by code hash. When the NFT sells, its account, balance, stake, and items transfer automatically—and it earns 5% NEP-199 royalties.

Plus you built a ?judge proof page and zero-wallet 'Try it free' browser onboarding. Very high NEAR-native craft.

picks.name: Release Passport
picks.pitch: Software release authority as a NEP-171 NFT that is a keyless NEAR sub-account holding release hashes and a slashable bond.
picks.memo:
Release Passport turns software release authority (solving npm event-stream-style maintainer takeovers) into a NEP-171 NFT that is also a keyless NEAR sub-account holding a security bond and sha256 release manifests. Selling the NFT transfers publishing rights and the bond cleanly with zero leftover keys.

Running `node cli/rp-verify.mjs cli/rp-verify.mjs` against live testnet with zero wallet/keys is a slick 2-minute proof.

picks.name: Satchel
picks.pitch: NEP-171 NFT on NEAR testnet where each token owns native BTC, ETH, and SOL addresses via Chain Signatures—transfer the NFT, transfer the wallet.
picks.memo:
Satchel is one of the smartest uses of NEAR Chain Signatures in the hackathon. You normally cannot safely sell a crypto wallet because anyone who ever saw the seed phrase retains access; Satchel fixes that by making each NEP-171 NFT control its own native Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana addresses through NEAR MPC, so transferring or selling the NFT transfers control of the underlying multi-chain assets with no bridges or wrapped tokens.

The execution matches the idea: a live app at usesatchel.xyz, Rust contracts, a 60-second no-wallet judge flow, and honest testnet disclaimers. It's a standout primitive that showcases why NEAR's account/MPC model is uniquely suited for programmable ownership.

picks.name: NEARpedia
picks.pitch: Live 27-tool NEAR MCP server & web app (near-pedia.xyz) with `check_code` deprecation linting and live validator/proposal queries.
picks.memo:
Built by UnityNodes (same team as Psephex), NEARpedia is a genuinely useful ecosystem tool: a 27-tool MCP server that answers live mainnet validator/proposal queries AND runs `check_code` to catch outdated `near-sdk-js` / `keyStores` patterns in AI-generated code.

Live at `near-pedia.xyz` with CI, Sentry, and Vitest. More dev-tooling than novel protocol, which keeps it just below the 4.7+ protocol builds.

picks.name: Priced In: prediction markets for facts
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR USDC prediction-market encyclopedia where TEE-attested AI models adjudicate facts and rewrite articles from odds.
picks.memo:
Priced In is genuinely jaw-dropping: an encyclopedia on NEAR mainnet backed by real USDC prediction markets where every checkable sentence is a Yes/No market. When Wikipedia claimed Tether held $72.6B in T-Bills vs. Tether's $122.84B attestation, bets drove it to 10%, three TEE-attested AI models ruled it false on-chain, the contract verified their signatures and paid $4.93 to No, and the live page updated to $122.84B.

Live on mainnet with real USDC, 12-check CI on clean Linux, and a direct realization of Illia's market-driven truth thesis. Absolute Grand Prize material.

picks.name: RERUN
picks.pitch: Mainnet USDC forecasting market where an AI Lab reruns scientific papers' code/data in a sealed box and posts NEAR receipts.
picks.memo:
RERUN is one of the most original and complete builds in Batch Q: a forecasting market on whether published scientific studies replicate. Users stake predictions, and 'the Lab' (an AI agent) reruns the study's public code and data in a sealed box and posts a verifiable receipt on NEAR that anyone can audit.

Crucially, it is **live on NEAR mainnet with real USDC** (`rerun-mainnet.vercel.app`) alongside a testnet sandbox (`rerun-testnet.vercel.app`), backed by a full pnpm monorepo (`contracts`, `lab`, `rebuilds`, `claims`, `packages`), CI, and a demo video on X. Outstanding execution and real-world utility.

picks.name: Tidepool
picks.pitch: Community-operated, 1Click-compatible NEAR Intents testnet API running official `defuse` v0.4.2 so builders can test BTC/XRP/SUI/Stellar swaps without mainnet funds.
picks.memo:
Tidepool solves one of the biggest developer pain points of this entire hackathon: **there is no official testnet for NEAR Intents 1Click**, forcing devs to either mock or spend mainnet money. Tidepool runs a 1Click-compatible testnet API backed by the official `defuse` v0.4.2 verifier on NEAR testnet, with e2e scripts for BTC, Stellar, Sui, and XRP + `llms-full.txt`.

Pure ecosystem force-multiplier.

picks.name: Undo for Bitcoin: a cancel button for a stolen key
picks.pitch: Cancel button for stolen native Bitcoin keys using 2-of-2 NEAR Chain Signatures, a public wait contract, and iPhone passkey cancellation.
picks.memo:
Undo for Bitcoin is a standout technical achievement: it gives native Bitcoin a cancel button without trusting NEAR unilaterally. Bitcoin itself rejects a stolen spend key alone; the second key lives on NEAR Chain Signatures behind a public NEAR contract that enforces a wait period during which your iPhone's Safari Face ID passkey can cancel the spend—and if NEAR ever disappears, a cold key recovers the BTC after a Bitcoin timelock.

The repo (`contracts/`, `crates/`, `proofs/`, `CLAIMS.md`, `verify.sh`, plus a one-take iPhone Face ID vs. thief-tab film on `undo-btc.pages.dev`) is extraordinarily rigorous. It's testnet-only (Bitcoin testnet + NEAR testnet), which is the only thing keeping it from 4.8+.

picks.name: Antumbra
picks.pitch: Shielded pool with sealed-amount epoch batch swaps on NEAR using Groth16 (NEP-488), browser WASM proving, and OutLayer TEE clearing.
picks.memo:
This is one of the strongest engineering builds in the entire batch. Instead of wrapping an existing privacy tool, you built a full Rust workspace—Poseidon over BLS12-381, Groth16 join-split/swap/claim circuits, a shielded pool contract verified on-chain via NEAR NEP-488 host functions, a CLI, and a browser WASM prover in web/ that generates proofs in ~3 seconds.

What really separates Antumbra is the Day 7–10 work: sealing swap amounts so the chain only sees a commitment + ciphertext while OutLayer TEE clears each epoch batch at a single uniform price, plus dry-run batch pricing via NEAR Intents 1Click. The only reason this isn't a 5.00 is that the Intents 1Click integration is still dry-run pricing rather than live mainnet settlement, and ZK UX inherently carries proof-wait friction.

picks.name: Arrow
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet inspect-before-pay data market where NEAR AI TEEs return BUY/PASS verdicts on 40-row samples without leaking rows.
picks.memo:
Arrow solves the data-marketplace inspection paradox ('to judge data you must see it; once you've seen it, why pay?') live on NEAR mainnet: sellers list encrypted files, an AI inside NEAR AI's sealed hardware inspects a 40-row sample against the buyer's criteria, and the buyer receives only a BUY or PASS verdict with fit and novelty scores—never the raw rows.

With live Vercel UI (`arrow-market.vercel.app`), Rust `contracts/`, `bench/`, `JUDGES.md`, `STATUS.md`, passing CI, and zero-key mainnet operation, Arrow is one of the most complete, production-minded builds in the entire hackathon.

picks.name: Attested Arena
picks.pitch: Trustless AI model competition (`zavodil.github.io/attested-arena/`) re-verifying 631 TDX/Wasm checks against live NEAR testnet.
picks.memo:
Attested Arena solves benchmark contamination in AI model competitions: test sets stay sealed until the duel inside attested hardware, a NEAR contract handles prizes without trusted operators, and the live report (`zavodil.github.io/attested-arena/`) compiles the judge's Rust code to WebAssembly alongside Intel's quote verifier to re-run 631 checks directly in the judge's browser—with one button repeating them against live NEAR testnet state.

Exceptional engineering rigor (`contract`, `core`, `judge`, `probe`, `verify-web`, `verify`). Zero trust-me handwaving; easily the technical benchmark of Batch F.

picks.name: Bandsheet
picks.pitch: TEE-attested union pay-band publisher that blocks salary-differencing leaks and gates releases via NEAR DAO voting.
picks.memo:
Bandsheet solves a subtle, real-world privacy failure—differencing attacks across consecutive pay-band tables where adding one new hire leaks their exact salary by subtraction. Payslips are read inside a TEE, forged inputs are rejected, any table that would enable differencing is refused, and each release requires a union DAO vote on NEAR.

The engineering discipline is top-notch: `THREAT_MODEL.md`, `JUDGES.md`, `enclave/`, `contracts/`, `mcp/`, CI, a tagged `hackathon-submission` commit, and a demo video on synthetic union data. Testnet-only status is the only boundary.

picks.name: Blindspot
picks.pitch: Pre-prompt enclave verifier, on-chain enclave memory, and leak-mitigation CLI (`useblindspot`) for NEAR AI Cloud.
picks.memo:
Blindspot addresses a subtle gap in NEAR AI Cloud privacy: Intel TDX attestation covers four enclave images, not the model engine itself. Blindspot ships a pre-prompt verification gate, an on-chain enclave memory on NEAR testnet, a hardware-free alarm, and leak-mitigation tools—usable via `useblindspot.xyz`, `bunx useblindspot` (published on npm), and a keyless CLI. The repo includes `circuits/`, `contracts/`, `deployments/`, `evidence/`, `JUDGES.md`, and `THREAT_MODEL.md`.

Sharp, timely response to real confidential-compute limits; testnet-only is the main ceiling.

picks.name: Dark Vault: Pay Anywhere
picks.pitch: Mainnet sealed-bid auctions and settlement on Zcash shielded escrow funded from any chain via NEAR Intents.
picks.memo:
Dark Vault: Pay Anywhere bridges NEAR Intents into Zcash shielded escrow so bidders can participate in private sealed-bid auctions, order flow, and OTC settlement using USDC, ETH, SOL, BTC, or NEAR—with NEAR Intents swapping and delivering shielded ZEC.

The cryptographic design is serious: time-locked shielded deposits so not even the site can open bids early, round-amount deposit padding to hide bid size from the operator, browser-verified proofs that the highest bid won without revealing losing bids, and **live on mainnet**. A standout Privacy entry.

picks.name: FireKey
picks.pitch: Shielded Zcash vault + Baochip-1x hardware cap + NEAR Intents + mainnet NEAR contract for private agent payments.
picks.memo:
FireKey is a standout technical achievement in Batch Q: an AI agent's principal stays hidden in a shielded Zcash vault; when it needs to pay, only the approved amount crosses via NEAR Intents into USDC on NEAR, enforced by an on-chain NEAR contract and a physical Baochip-1x hardware device that holds the cap and requires a button press above threshold.

Crucially, this isn't just a slide deck—`evidence/mainnet.md` and `PROGRESS.md` document real **NEAR mainnet** execution with real funds and the Baochip hardware, backed by a full Rust workspace (`contracts`, `crates`, `agent`, `docker`). Exceptional privacy + hardware + mainnet proof.

picks.name: Laurel
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet model competition where models are scored on a private OutLayer TEE test set and paid per prediction.
picks.memo:
Laurel tackles AI benchmark gaming with a live NEAR mainnet deployment (`laurel.ikantongkolmangut.near`, using `outlayer.near` as its TEE): small models are scored against a private test set held as an OutLayer mainnet secret inside a TEE, the winning model lives in a smart contract, and AI agents pay it per prediction.

The engineering rigor is exceptional—verified mainnet and testnet contracts with matching code hash (`BVNELFch…`), GitHub Actions test badges, `CLAIMS.md`, `SPIKE_LOG.md`, `contracts/`, `crates/`, and `evaluator/`. It is a genuinely novel, live-on-mainnet use of OutLayer TEEs and NEAR contracts.

picks.name: NEAR Privacy Rings
picks.pitch: Groth16 (`alt_bn128`) ZK shielded pool on NEAR with relayerless sends, private Rhea swaps, cross-chain deposits, and TEE agents.
picks.memo:
NEAR Privacy Rings is a powerhouse zero-knowledge shielded pool on NEAR using Groth16 proofs verified on-chain via NEAR's `alt_bn128` precompile. It supports encrypted NEAR/NEP-141 balances, relayerless anonymous sends via a published open-ring signing key, private atomic Rhea swaps, cross-chain deposits (SOL, ETH, BTC, Base, Arbitrum) without a NEAR account, and private AI agents driven by TEE-verified models.

The repo includes `circuits/`, `ceremony/`, `artifacts/`, `contract/`, `relayer/`, `open-ring/`, and `agent/`. Only a live mainnet URL is missing from the opening README excerpt to push it even higher.

picks.name: NTK - Near The Keyboard
picks.pitch: Android keyboard sealing keystroke biometrics in a NEAR OutLayer Intel TDX enclave to stamp and verify human-typed text (ntk.tools).
picks.memo:
NTK (Near The Keyboard) tackles AI-text impersonation from a hardware-enclave angle: a custom Android keyboard measures keystroke dynamics as you type, sends the measurements sealed into an Intel TDX enclave on NEAR OutLayer, and stamps matching text with a verifiable tag like [NTK 26144e35e7]. Anyone can verify the stamp at ntk.tools without seeing the underlying biometric fingerprint.

Supporting both NEAR testnet and mainnet with full android, enclave, relay, client, and web directories—and even using the stamp in its own X submission—makes this one of the most original and complete Privacy & Private AI builds in the batch.

picks.name: Rahasya
picks.pitch: Accountless private AI chat on Cloudflare Workers funded via NEAR Intents/shielded Zcash with browser-verified TEE mode.
picks.memo:
Rahasya (`rahasya.chat`, live on Cloudflare Workers) combines permissionless cross-chain payments with hardware-enforced AI privacy: users pay for uncensored/abliterated models using almost any token via NEAR Intents—including directly from a shielded Zcash pool so payer identity stays private—without an account or subscription. Its 'Truly private' mode runs strictly on hardware TEEs, encrypts messages in-browser, and surfaces attestation checks.

With live docs, `/llms-full.txt`, `SECURITY.md`, and `npm test` support, Rahasya executes both the payment-privacy and compute-privacy halves of the track cleanly.

picks.name: Sealed Ledger
picks.pitch: Private expense & receipt auditor running in NEAR AI Cloud Intel TDX + NVIDIA TEEs with downloadable proof.json.
picks.memo:
Sealed Ledger turns NEAR AI Cloud confidential TEEs into an immediately usable product: upload receipt photos and bank CSVs (held in memory for one request), get anomaly detection + expense categorization, and download `proof.json` proving Intel TDX + NVIDIA hardware attestation.

Having a preconfigured live demo (`sealed-ledger.vercel.app/app`) with a 1-click 'Load sample' button that completes in ~40s makes judging effortless.

picks.name: Sieve
picks.pitch: Verifiable 3-TEE NEAR AI Cloud grant reviewer with on-chain prompt reconstruction and 3,895-review red-team validation.
picks.memo:
