Sieve solves AI grant-review gaming with serious rigor: three models inside NEAR AI Cloud TEEs score each proposal against an on-chain rubric, a NEAR contract rebuilds the exact prompt and verifies each enclave signature, and payouts follow a staged milestone model (0.2 NEAR newcomer cap before delivery, then 1 NEAR). Their red-team benchmark across **3,895 signed reviews** is standout: 0 of 10 static injection types passed, 19/20 good proposals still passed, and even an attacker LLM writing custom injections dropped from 56% bypass on a naive prompt to 11%.

The remaining 11% adaptive-attacker bypass is honestly reported rather than hidden, and it's testnet-only, but the combination of TEE multi-model judging, on-chain prompt reconstruction, and 3,895-run red-teaming is top-3 material.

picks.name: Sightline
picks.pitch: Zero-storage document reader for blind/low-vision users running inside an attested Intel TDX enclave on NEAR AI Cloud.
picks.memo:
Sightline addresses a deeply human privacy problem: blind and low-vision users often must ask someone else to read sensitive documents aloud. Sightline processes documents inside an attested Intel TDX enclave on NEAR AI Cloud, returning signed answers while keeping 0 KB on the server (in-memory only).

The engineering quality is among the highest in the hackathon: 938 Vitest unit/integration tests, 164 Playwright E2E tests, CI, OpenSSF Scorecard badge, and `HACKATHON.md` / `ARCHITECTURE_ESSENTIALS.md`. Its main limitation is relying on NEAR AI Cloud TEE without custom on-chain smart contracts, which fits the track well nonetheless.

picks.name: Skarbnik
picks.pitch: Private AI patch-bounty protocol (`skarbnik.xyz`) verifying secret exploit tests in a RISC zkVM with on-chain Groth16 settlement.
picks.memo:
Skarbnik enables private bug-repair bounties for AI agents: security teams post a bug with a secret test input, agents submit patches via MCP without ever seeing the exploit input, a RISC zkVM evaluates the patch and emits a Groth16 proof (`PASS`/`FAIL`), and the NEAR contract (`kintsugi-l2-cihdp.testnet`) verifies the proof and releases the bounty.

Everything a judge wants is present: live site (`skarbnik.xyz`), `JUDGE_GUIDE.md`, MCP support, CI, 2-minute demo video, and an on-chain testnet verifier. The only caveat is that it runs on NEAR testnet rather than mainnet.

picks.name: SPHINX
picks.pitch: Mainnet sealed-information market (`asksphinx.xyz`) combining OutLayer TEE private AI Q&A with single-tx hidden-price settlement.
picks.memo:
Sphinx solves Arrow's information paradox—how to buy a secret (a bug finding, dataset, or research) you can't inspect before paying—using an OutLayer TEE sealed box and a NEAR mainnet contract (`7c3bcf93...cee9681`). Buyers interrogate the sealed box with yes/no questions answered by a private AI inside secure hardware, both sides submit hidden bids, and overlapping prices settle at a hidden random midpoint in one NEAR transaction with full refund on failure.

Having both the contract and the OutLayer sealed box live on NEAR mainnet at `asksphinx.xyz`, backed by `contract/`, `enclave/`, `agent/`, `scripts/`, and `web/`, puts Sphinx at the very top of the hackathon.

picks.name: Yield AI Agent
picks.pitch: E2EE TEE-backed yield advisor (yieldai.app/agent) using NEAR AI Cloud and NEAR Intents where earned USDC yield pays for AI credits.
picks.memo:
Yield AI Agent pairs end-to-end encrypted private chat on NEAR AI Cloud TEE (so the operator cannot inspect user balances or financial plans) with an on-chain USDC yield account via NEAR Intents 1-Click and Solana Safe, plus a fee meter that converts earned yield directly into AI inference credits.

It ships a live demo (`yieldai.app/agent`) and a 2:15 video walkthrough, backed by a clean Next.js/TypeScript repo. The self-sustaining 'yield pays for private AI' economic loop is one of the most cohesive product concepts in Batch K.

picks.name: Accord
picks.pitch: Mainnet native-USDC B2B purchase-order escrow (accord-payments.vercel.app) with supplier term lock and delivery-gated partial payouts.
picks.memo:
Accord is a B2B purchase-order and delivery-confirmed settlement platform live on NEAR mainnet with native USDC (`accord-payments.vercel.app`): AI prepares invoice details for review, suppliers confirm terms before buyers fund orders, buyers (or appointed receivers) confirm delivery, and the Rust NEAR contract enforces partial settlement, mutual closure, and native-deposit refunds.

The repo (`MAINNET_RELEASE.md`, `SECURITY_REVIEW.md`, `FOUNDATION.md`, `JUDGE.md`, `NATIVE_DEPOSITS.md`) documents a verified live mainnet USDC order with controlled 3 NEAR cap. Real mainnet USDC execution plus thorough security documentation puts Accord at the top of the batch.

picks.name: Fulfil: NEAR Intents for real-life orders
picks.pitch: Mainnet NEAR USDC escrow where OutLayer TEE verifiers (including DKIM bank-email proofs) settle real-world orders in seconds.
picks.memo:
Fulfil is a textbook hackathon winner. Instead of just swapping tokens, you extended the Intent model to real-world fulfillment: a buyer locks real USDC in nearfullfil.near on NEAR mainnet, a human/bot/agent fulfills a real-world job (VietQR bank transfer, mobile top-up, in-person QR handoff, or token buy), and a verifier inside a NEAR OutLayer TEE checks the DKIM-signed bank email or chain proof before releasing escrow.

What puts this at the very top: you didn't stop at testnet slides—you have real mainnet transaction hashes on nearfullfil.near (e.g. a 3.96s TEE DKIM verification paying out a VietQR transfer, and an 84s autonomous bot top-up), PLUS a wallet-free /demo mode so any judge can test it in 2 minutes. My only caution is operational scalability of fulfiller liquidity and dispute edge cases on DKIM failures, but as a hackathon build, this is exceptional.

picks.name: Panda Pay Africa: USDC Checkout
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live WhatsApp cross-chain USDC checkout via NEAR Intents with an on-chain refund-cap policy contract.
picks.memo:
Panda Pay Africa ships a cross-chain USDC WhatsApp checkout live on NEAR mainnet (`policy.afropanda.near`), using NEAR Intents (1Click) to swap customer USDC from Solana, Ethereum, or Base into USDC on NEAR for merchants. Every settled payment is recorded on the NEAR spending-guard contract—which has a verifiable release code hash (`HoV3wZrvHBAnCmVMYiQ3tpnTh4vTwUMT1CiBnBDQm56g`), mainnet deploy tx, and a function-call-scoped `operator.afropanda.near` key that caps refunds per payment.

The repo also includes `BENCHMARKS.md`, `agent-harness/`, `checkout-policy/`, `intents-checkout/`, and Docker setup. A standout real-world commerce build.

picks.name: Paya
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live fiat on/off-ramp between bank accounts and NEAR with email sign-in and auto cash-out.
picks.memo:
Paya is live on **NEAR mainnet** with real money at `usepaya.xyz/app`, enabling users to buy NEAR with bank transfers (e.g., Nigerian Naira), cash out NEAR to a bank account, or turn on auto cash-out using email sign-in or standard NEAR wallets (HOT, Meteor, Nightly). The repo includes `contracts/`, `services/`, `frontend/`, `admin/`, `docs/`, and `examples/`.

Shipping a working, no-access-code mainnet fiat on/off-ramp with real bank settlement is a high bar for Real-World Money, trailing Panda Pay Africa only slightly on surfaced contract-hash/refund-guard verification details.

picks.name: Payminto
picks.pitch: Self-hosted, non-custodial NEAR Intents payment gateway settling multi-chain payments and MCP agent budgets into merchant NEAR USDC.
picks.memo:
Payminto is a self-hosted, non-custodial payment gateway on NEAR Intents: merchants share a link/QR, buyers pay from Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Solana, or Polygon, and exact USDC lands in the merchant's own NEAR account (demonstrated Base-to-NEAR in 36 seconds on mainnet in the 2:19 YouTube demo).

It also extends cleanly to AI agents via Budgets and MCP tools (`docs/media/payminto-agents.mp4`), backed by a full pnpm monorepo (`apps/`, `contracts-near/`, `packages/`, `docker-compose.yml`). Requiring self-hosting via Docker is slightly heavier for casual testers than a hosted SaaS link, but the architecture and mainnet proof are top-notch.

picks.name: Penstock
picks.pitch: Any-chain x402 paywall for HTTP APIs and MCP tools settling into seller USDC on NEAR via NEAR Intents (mainnet-proven).
picks.memo:
Penstock turns any HTTP API or MCP tool into an x402 paywall where AI agents can pay with any token on any chain and sellers always receive clean USDC in one NEAR account via NEAR Intents. Crucially, this isn't just a testnet mock—the demo video shows a real mainnet payment from Solana plus a real refund.

The pnpm monorepo (`apps`, `packages`, `examples`, `wrangler.toml`, `vitest.config.ts`) looks production-minded and directly addresses the multi-chain fragmentation problem for agent-accessible APIs. A top-tier Real-World Money / Agent Economy bridge.

picks.name: Rajista Pay on NEAR
picks.pitch: Mainnet Nigerian retail POS (`rajistapay.near`) accepting multi-chain USDC/USDT via NEAR Intents and settling USDC on NEAR.
picks.memo:
Rajista Pay is a textbook Real-World Money build: a shop in Kano, Nigeria rings up a sale in Naira and displays a QR; the customer pays in USDC/USDT from any of 10 chains (Base, Solana, Arbitrum, Tron, etc.); NEAR Intents converts it; and the NEAR invoice contract settles USDC to the merchant with CSV bookkeeping export.

Crucially, it is **live on NEAR mainnet** (`rajistapay.near`, `rajista-pay.rajista.workers.dev`) and documented a **real mainnet sale** on Nov 12, 2026 in Kano (customer paid from Base, settled on NEAR) with a public receipt link and video.

picks.name: Recurra - crypto payments & subscriptions for WooCommerce on NEAR
picks.pitch: WooCommerce recurring-billing plugin with a NEAR mainnet vault contract and cross-chain NEAR Intents 1Click funding.
picks.memo:
Recurra tackles a notoriously hard crypto UX gap—recurring subscriptions—with a real WooCommerce plugin (`wp-plugin`) backed by a NEAR **mainnet** vault contract (`Recurra Vault`). Customers prepay N periods with a strict on-chain rule (max X per period, merchant-only destination, cancel anytime for a refund) and can fund from Arbitrum, Base, Ethereum, or Solana via NEAR Intents 1Click.

Shipping mainnet execution, a WooCommerce integration, `charger`, `docker`, and an 8-minute mainnet Base-to-NEAR checkout demo makes this a standout real-world commerce build.

picks.name: Settl
picks.pitch: Mainnet-live (`settl-billonaire.near`) freelancer crypto invoicing: clients pay in any asset via NEAR Intents and collaborators receive auto-split USDC on NEAR.
picks.memo:
Settl (by ZSP111, who also built Heir) is **live on NEAR mainnet with real USDC** (`settl-billonaire.near`) AND has a separate testnet sandbox (`settl-billonaire.testnet`). Freelancers send an invoice link, clients pay with BTC/ETH/SOL/USDC via NEAR Intents, and payouts auto-split (e.g. 70/30) with optional escrow.

Shipping on mainnet with real receipts puts this right near the top of Real-World Money.

picks.name: Earmark
picks.pitch: Zero-key NEAR mainnet budget contract (`budgets.omkar5.near`) owned by a Sputnik DAO for delegated USDC spending.
picks.memo:
Earmark tackles a documented NEAR ecosystem pain point—DAOs voting on every tiny payout (citing 14,171 proposals)—by letting a Sputnik/Trezu DAO vote once on a budget enforced by a zero-key NEAR mainnet contract (`budgets.omkar5.near`, owned by `earmark.sputnik-dao.near`) using native USDC.

With a live Cloud Run mainnet app, CI + live-check workflows, `JUDGE.md`, and a single-command `make verify NET=mainnet` check, this is one of the cleanest, most production-minded builds in the batch.

picks.name: Headcount
picks.pitch: Sybil-screening payout router for Sputnik DAO and Trezu treasuries verified against mainnet DAO bytecode in sandbox.
picks.memo:
Headcount protects Sputnik DAO and Trezu reward rounds from sybil splitting: it inspects on-chain NEAR history for each recipient in a Trezu-format CSV, pays clearly independent accounts, and routes linked account clusters to a council vote.

The engineering verification is top-notch: 125 TypeScript tests and 122 Rust unit tests running in `near-workspaces` sandbox against the exact mainnet Sputnik DAO v3.2 bytecode (code-hash verified). Currently sandbox-only rather than hosted live on testnet.

picks.name: Ringfence
picks.pitch: Voice and WhatsApp NEAR wallet/red-packet app (`ringfence.evalengine.ai`) backed by per-phone-number mainnet spending-cap contracts.
picks.memo:
Ringfence gives an AI a NEAR wallet and a phone number: you call in a browser or on WhatsApp, say 'send 0.1 NEAR to liho.near' or 'make a money packet for 3 people, the words are good morning', and confirm with a spoken PIN. Crucially, every phone number has its own NEAR contract capping per-transfer limits, daily limits, and saved recipients—so the AI only proposes while the contract enforces.

Live demo (`ringfence.evalengine.ai`), 64s film, self-host docs, and real **NEAR mainnet** money-packet payouts make this one of the most memorable Social Money builds in the batch.

picks.name: Stated
picks.pitch: Keyless NEAR mainnet escrow (`escrow.statedforecast.near`) and 3-model AI jury settling X-reply bets.
picks.memo:
Stated turns any X claim into a two-party bet held by a keyless NEAR mainnet contract (`escrow.statedforecast.near`) and adjudicated by a three-model AI jury (`referee.statedforecast.near`). It shipped real mainnet settlements on Nov 14, 2026, a live Railway app, `JUDGE.md`, `DESIGN.md`, and a reproducible `verify-mainnet-demo.mjs` script (`PASS mainnet demo: 2/2 cases; 15/15 checks`).

I appreciate the candor in explicitly noting that the mainnet path does not yet verify per-model enclave attestation and that the settled mainnet trials were between the team's own accounts.

picks.name: Warden
picks.pitch: Sputnik DAO payout vault on NEAR testnet gating AI agent disbursements behind caps, earned trust, council votes, and a TEE judge.
picks.memo:
Warden (`itsharshag.github.io/near-warden/`) lets a community delegate contributor payouts to an AI agent while keeping treasury custody in a Sputnik DAO. Payouts must clear on-chain caps, earned contributor trust, council/DAO votes, and a signed TEE judge—demonstrated in two videos (46s booth + 100s testnet attack-stopped run) and backed by 20 passing contract tests, `evidence/`, `verifier/`, and `mcp/`.

It bridges Social Money, AI Security, and Agent Economy with concrete testnet proof and a live dashboard.

picks.name: Blindbook
picks.pitch: Intel TDX dark pool for NEAR Intents (`pool.blindbook.near`) settling matched block orders atomically on `intents.near` mainnet.
picks.memo:
Blindbook is a dark pool (block-crossing venue) for NEAR Intents, solving a concrete institutional pain point documented right in its X post (150k NEAR costing 102 bps on public Intents). Traders seal block orders at their limit; an Intel TDX enclave matcher crosses opposing sides at a 1Click-signed midpoint and settles both legs atomically in one `execute_intents` call on `intents.near`, keeping resting orders hidden from solvers and other traders.

**Live on NEAR mainnet** (`pool.blindbook.near`, verified mainnet tx `5HgpGzUbGPENVWwcf5kQNgWX2hMCTJSMqrjhGky4UFiZ` settling 0.1 NEAR lots at 3.73253 USDC mid) with `CLAIMS.md`, `JUDGES.md`, `results`, `matcher`, and `contracts`. Easily the strongest technical + mainnet-proven entry in Batch D.

picks.name: Counterweight
picks.pitch: Keyless NEAR mainnet policy (0 access keys) that opened/closed a Hyperliquid short and returned USDC on Arbitrum.
picks.memo:
Counterweight executed a complete, verifiable **NEAR + Hyperliquid MAINNET** lifecycle on 14 Nov 2026: its keyless policy contract (`cw4.haxheton.near`, verified 0 access keys on NearBlocks) custodied 3.6 wNEAR, signed a 3.6 NEAR short on Hyperliquid via NEAR signature, executed a reduce-only close, and withdrew `17.886709` native USDC to the fixed owner recipient on Arbitrum One.

The team is exemplary in stating verification limits—owner-supervised, tiny size, one lifecycle, unaudited, no autonomous mainnet keeper. Real mainnet cross-chain MPC execution with zero access keys makes it the highest-conviction DeFi build in Batch T.

picks.name: FairWarning
picks.pitch: Trustless admin-key watchdog where NEAR MPC `verify_foreign_transaction` reads Base logs and slashes a NEAR USDC bond if upgrades skip notice.
picks.memo:
Fair Warning solves a real DeFi trust gap with an unusually sharp NEAR-native primitive: a team keeps its instant EVM admin key on Base, promises N blocks of advance notice before any upgrade or role grant, and backs that promise with a USDC bond on NEAR out of reach of the admin key. If the key acts without notice, anyone can prove it—NEAR reads the EVM log directly via the MPC network's `verify_foreign_transaction` and slashes the bond (10% to the reporter, 90% to depositors) with zero external bridges or oracle committees.

The repo includes `contracts`, `backend`, `tools`, `web`, `AGENTS.md`, and live testnet deployment. It's one of the best uses of NEAR's foreign-transaction MPC verification in the entire hackathon; only testnet-only status keeps it slightly shy of a mainnet-proven 4.8+.

picks.name: Lifeline
picks.pitch: Production-grade automated margin rescue for Hyperliquid traders funded cross-chain via NEAR Intents, with a verified mainnet rescue.
picks.memo:
LifeLine is one of the most complete engineering submissions in the entire hackathon. It solves a real, high-stakes DeFi pain point—getting liquidated in your sleep on Hyperliquid—by holding a reserve on NEAR and bridging margin top-ups via NEAR Intents. Crucially, this isn't just testnet theater: the vault is deployed on NEAR mainnet (vault.lifeline-hq.near) with a documented first mainnet rescue of 1.68 USDC landing on Hyperliquid in 48.6 seconds.

The repository hygiene is exceptional, featuring GitHub Actions CI, 1,550 TypeScript tests plus 62 contract tests, SECURITY.md, ROADMAP.md, research/mainnet/RESCUE.md, and a live demo at lifeline.prashantthakur.dev. The only minor caveats are that a 48.6-second cross-chain rescue can still be tight during violent flash crashes, and real-money vault security always warrants a formal third-party audit.

picks.name: Nomad
picks.pitch: Atomic multi-standard (`nep413`/`erc191`/`ed25519`) ring-trading settlement on NEAR Intents verified against `intents.near` Wasm.
picks.memo:
Nomad solves multi-party coincidence-of-wants across agents and wallets: each participant signs only its own leg (`nep413`, `erc191`, and `raw_ed25519` all mixed in the same ring), anyone can close the ring, and NEAR Intents settles the entire loop atomically in one transaction with zero access keys on the rings and mandate contracts.

The engineering proof is top-shelf: the verifier runs `intents.near`'s exact mainnet Wasm code hash, 27 rings settled with 0 failures in a 36-minute live run of 12 agents, 125 TS + 70 Rust tests run in CI, plus a live site (`nomad.charlesms.dev`), X video, and one-command keyless `make demo`.

picks.name: Origami Verse
picks.pitch: Multiverse conditional-outcome tokens on NEAR testnet backed by 856 passing Rust tests, oracle tooling, and a whitepaper.
picks.memo:
Origami Verse implements multiverse conditional tokens on NEAR testnet (`app.ifverse-staging.testnet`): pick 1–3 real-world events and split 1 wNEAR into one NEAR-if-world token per outcome combination, each paying out only if its world comes true. The engineering rigor is remarkable: Rust `near-sdk 5.14` contracts, **856 passing Rust tests**, `oracle/`, `crates/`, `deployments/`, a Next.js 16 UI (`multiverse-lending.vercel.app`), docs, and a full PDF whitepaper.

Remaining on testnet is the only thing keeping it from a 4.7+ score.

picks.name: Parity
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet Gaussian pm-AMM implementing options-instead-of-debt (Borrow, Multiply, Earn) with zero-custody TDX Shade Agent quotes.
picks.memo:
Parity ships Vitalik Buterin's 'options instead of debt' design **live on NEAR mainnet** (`parity-core.near`): a single shared Gaussian pm-AMM pool powers Borrow, Multiply, and Earn, while a TDX Shade Agent signs quotes with zero custody. It backs this up with a live app (`parity-protocol.vercel.app`), a live TDX hardware attestation endpoint (`/api/tdx/attestation`), `PROTOCOL_ABI_SPEC.md`, and a 4:42 mainnet demo video.

Mainnet deployment of a genuinely novel DeFi primitive combined with verifiable TDX Shade Agent quotes puts Parity at the very top of Batch N.

picks.name: Ripcord
picks.pitch: Live NEAR mainnet TEE + private Intents reserve that rescues Hyperliquid positions before public liquidation.
picks.memo:
Ripcord (`ripcord-self.vercel.app`) solves a real, high-stakes DeFi problem: Hyperliquid liquidation prices are public and routinely hunted. Ripcord seals a hidden trigger inside a NEAR TEE, holds a private reserve in NEAR Intents, and automatically lands margin on Hyperliquid in under a minute—with strict owner-only payout guarantees.

It is live on NEAR mainnet with a 3-minute video showing a real mainnet margin rescue executed in 26 seconds, plus a zero-funds simulation mode for judges.

picks.name: Silent Partner
picks.pitch: Mainnet real-USDC sealed copy-trading vault on NEAR using MPC signatures to eliminate follower frontrunning.
picks.memo:
Silent Partner tackles copy-trading frontrunning by pooling leader and followers into one sealed vault, executing one fill at one price via an MPC-signed shield transaction so positions are never exposed before execution. Crucially, it is live on **NEAR mainnet with real USDC**, complete with verifiable mainnet deposit, private trade, and follower payout transactions.

The vault contract's deployed code hash (`9S9R3aaEs3cPs9nyjvhZKnsK7Ry3GcHTi1f1KVBtZy34`) matches its reproducible build (`docs/mainnet.md`), and the repo includes `contract/`, `extension/`, `operator/`, `registry/`, and `web/`. This is top-tier mainnet execution.

picks.name: Warrant
picks.pitch: Oracle-free, non-defaulting options locking collateral in NEAR Intents, deployed and source-verified on NEAR mainnet (`warrant-options.near`).
picks.memo:
Warrant builds oracle-free, non-defaulting options by locking option collateral directly inside NEAR Intents until expiry—eliminating both seller default risk and oracle manipulation. Even better, it is deployed live on **NEAR mainnet** (`warrant-options.near`) with NearBlocks-verified source code and a locked contract.

Backed by 78 unit tests, 4 integration tests against real Intents bytecode, green CI, `contracts/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, and `web/`. Shipping a locked, source-verified mainnet DeFi primitive puts Warrant at the very top of the batch.
